 Top court rejects extended tax deadlines
 [Intime News] 
 Newsroom 
 October 30, 2026 
 30.10.2026 • 20:55 
 The Council of State, Greece’s supreme administrative court, has restricted the government’s ability to impose taxes and penalties in older cases, ruling that extended limitation periods violate constitutional principles.
 In decision 1246/2026, a seven-member panel of the court’s Second Chamber found unconstitutional the 10-year limitation period introduced under Law 4646/2019 for certain earlier tax periods. It also invalidated the 20-year period for tax evasion cases.
 The court said deadlines must comply with proportionality and legal certainty, noting that modern electronic auditing tools and risk-analysis systems reduce the need for lengthy periods.
 The ruling covers the 2012 and 2013 financial years and tax years 2014 through 2017. Cases relying solely on the invalidated 10-year provision must close if the standard five-year limitation period has expired and no lawful exception applies.
 The decision followed a dispute involving a honey-producing business fined €4,640 in 2020 for receiving a fictitious invoice worth €11,600 in 2013. The court concluded that the penalty deadline had expired on December 31, 2019.
 It rejected the tax authority’s argument that the 2019 law had favorably reduced the previous 20-year period to 10 years.
